title: RANK 2: independent re-execution of the 27 RC-8 S-box draws

inference.model_verified_reason: no adapter probe is available in this harness; the resolved model is reported from the runtime identity, not from a probe

claim_tier_basis: Reduced-round AES-128 permutation, r=5, one machine, 2^30 trials per draw, 27 drawn bijective S-boxes. Nothing here is a statement about full-round or deployed AES and no comparison to published cryptanalysis is made in either direction (RQ-AES-003 R3). A timeout or a killed process is resource exhaustion, never negative evidence.

certificate.basis: pure measurement run; no discrete-log solve and no factor-base relation is claimed

WHAT_THIS_REPLICATES.target: BATCH-006 TASK-20260803-0764fc, RANK 2 (RC-8): 27 random bijective S-box draws measured at r=5, 2^30 trials, arm seed 631001.
WHAT_THIS_REPLICATES.why: That bound rested on one implementation in one session. The BATCH-006 validator intended to re-execute it, hit ~10.6 h against a 4800 s budget, and named the omission (EV-AES-9794e1 unresolved_confounds[0]).
WHAT_THIS_REPLICATES.same_objects: The SAME 27 S-box seeds 20260803701..20260803727, the same arm seed 631001, armid 1, 2 threads, log2N 30, rounds 5, amask 1, smask 1. The draw, key derivation, per-thread split and trial stream are deterministic functions of these, so a correct implementation must reproduce the counts integer for integer. This is bit-exact replication on the same sample, NOT an independent resampling; replicating different draws would answer a different question.
WHAT_THIS_REPLICATES.sampling_noise_is_not_an_available_expla: Because the sample is not redrawn, a count disagreement cannot be charged to sampling. It would be an instrument fault in one of the two implementations, or a real divergence.

INSTRUMENT.name: rc8probe
INSTRUMENT.why_two_binaries: rc8probe (-O3) was built and pinned first; rc8probe_native (-O3 -march=native -funroll-loops) measured ~6% faster on the 2^24 benchmark and was re-pinned against FIPS-197 C.1 before being used. Both pins are recorded. Every reported count comes from rc8probe_native.
deliberate_differences_from_BATCH004_yoy: No T-tables: state is 16 bytes and SubBytes / ShiftRows / MixColumns / AddRoundKey are four separate byte-level steps with small GF(2^8) multiply tables (mul2, mul3, mul9, mul11, mul13, mul14). yoyo_sbox_v2 fuses SB+SR+MC into four 32-bit T-tables.

Direct inverse cipher (ARK, InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes, InvMixColumns in straight reversed order, forward round keys only). yoyo_sbox_v2 uses the equivalent inverse cipher with InvMixColumns-transformed round keys and U-tables.
AES S-box built from log/antilog tables over generator 0x03 with the affine map as a byte-rotation identity. yoyo_sbox_v2 finds the GF(2^8) inverse by an O(256^2) product search.
Word-oriented key expansion with explicit RotWord/SubWord/Rcon over 44 4-byte words, rather than the fused byte loop.
deliberately_reproduced_because_they_def: the plaintext / active-word draw and its rejection condition
key derivation kst = seed ^ 0xA5A5A5A5A5A5A5A5 then two splitmix64 draws
the per-thread trial split N/nthr with the remainder on thread 0
INSTRUMENT.provenance_of_the_conventions: Read from BATCH-006's yoyo_sbox_v2.c.readonly_copy, which the card permits in order to learn what object is measured. The code is newly written.

P1_fips197_c1_known_answer_vector.note: run BEFORE any measurement; the same enc_r/dec_r are used to measure

P2_bijectivity_and_P3_roundtrip_and_P4_s.meaning: P4 establishes independently of any count that the two implementations draw the SAME S-box from each seed, so a count disagreement could not be blamed on drawing a different object.

P5_cross_implementation_anchor_at_2^24.result: EXACT agreement on trivial_swaps_excluded, nontrivial_trials, W_ge1_nontrivial (=2), W_ge1_by_word ([0,0,2,0]), whist, key_hex (c17835e6ca6233347781f4ba00d26ee4), thread_seeds and sbox_first8.
P5_cross_implementation_anchor_at_2^24.note: The archived binary was run ONLY as a check on my own code before measuring. No reported number comes from it.

P6_per_arm_pin_gate.description: Every `arm` invocation re-verifies dec_r(enc_r(x))==x under the S-box it is about to measure, 64 random (key,plaintext) pairs at every r in 1..10 = 640 checks, and refuses to measure on failure (exit 5). No arm exited 5.
P6_per_arm_pin_gate.note: The FIPS-197 C.1 vector is applicable only to the AES S-box and is never faked for a drawn S-box.

PINS_AND_VALIDITY_CHECKS.estimator_selftest_meaning: My Clopper-Pearson bisection recomputes BATCH-006's published bound 0.784700038857546 from k=25,n=27 to within 1e-12, and my upward-summed Poisson tail reproduces BATCH-006's published tails for X=9 and X=6. The estimator is therefore not a source of any difference in the bound.

THE_CRITERION.statement: ALIVE iff X/v >= 5 AND P(K >= X | lambda = v) < 1e-6.
THE_CRITERION.why_only_one: CORR-20260803-2cefa6 records that this is the ONLY criterion this campaign ever froze, and that BATCH-005's looser 'at least 5x' form presents itself in its own text as a QUOTATION of this rule while dropping the Poisson conjunct. A defective restatement does not create a rule. No second reading, no 'not DEAD' reading and no pooled bound is computed or reported here: reporting two readings side by side is how this campaign came to claim a 0.90 bound it had not earned.
THE_CRITERION.v_definition: v = nontrivial_trials * 4 / 2^32, the matched analytic null
THE_CRITERION.bound_estimator: one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound on ALIVE/n, solving sum_{j=k}^{n} C(n,j) p^j (1-p)^(n-j) = 0.05 by bisection; for k=n it is 0.05^(1/n)

PER_DRAW_AGREEMENT_SUMMARY.aggregate_is_not_the_deliverable: The per-draw verdicts above are the deliverable. This block is an index into them, not a substitute: aggregate agreement can hide compensating errors.

RESULT.bound_scope: p = fraction of bijective S-boxes that are ALIVE under the strict BATCH-004 rule at THIS round count (r=5), THIS key block (arm seed 631001), THIS exposure (2^30 trials) and THIS liveness rule. Unpooled, over the draws this task actually measured.

FINDING.headline: THE 27 RC-8 DRAWS REPLICATE EXACTLY ON A SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY WRITTEN INSTRUMENT. All 27 completed. All 27 agree with BATCH-006 integer for integer on W_ge1_nontrivial, trivial_swaps_excluded, W_ge1_by_word and the full whist, and on key_hex, thread_seeds and sbox_first8. ALIVE = 25 of 27 under the strict frozen BATCH-004 criterion, and the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound recomputes to 0.7847000388575458.
what_this_does_and_does_not_settle: SETTLED: the 0.7847 bound is no longer a one-implementation, one-session number. A second instrument, written for this task with no T-tables, a different inverse cipher, a different AES S-box construction and a different key-expansion loop, returns the same integers on the same 27 objects. The unresolved confound EV-AES-9794e1 unresolved_confounds[0] -- 'the 27 RC-8 arms were not independently re-executed' -- is addressed by this run.

NOT SETTLED: this is IMPLEMENTATION and SESSION independence, not MODEL independence. Both this task and BATCH-006 resolved to claude-opus-5 under standing basis 0137a051eb5828789eb267fa83c8278086578d4c with fallback_used true. Nothing here contributes a distinct resolved model to any closure quorum.

NOT SETTLED: exact agreement was the PREREGISTERED prediction and is a check on the two implementations, not new evidence about S-boxes. The sample was not redrawn, so the 27 draws bound the preserving fraction exactly as much as they did before; what changed is that the instrument reading them is no longer single.
OUT OF SCOPE: nothing here speaks to full-round or deployed AES, and no comparison to published cryptanalysis is made in either direction.
FINDING.if_the_bound_had_differed: It did not. Had it differed, the registered protocol was to report the difference as the finding and not reconcile it by adopting BATCH-006's numbers; PREREGISTRATION.md records that ladder in advance.

PROTOCOL_DEVIATIONS_AND_INCIDENTS.detail: rc8probe (-O3) was pinned first; rc8probe_native (-O3 -march=native -funroll-loops) benchmarked ~6% faster at 2^24 and was re-pinned against FIPS-197 C.1 before use. All 27 reported arms come from rc8probe_native. Both pin outputs are retained (runs/pin_aes.json, runs/pin_aes_native.json).

The tool wrapper that launched driver.sh returned exit code 1 while the detached driver.sh ran normally to completion (DRIVER_EXIT recorded, 27 arms, all exit=0). The exit status belonged to the launching shell, not to any measurement.

A guarded fallback was armed to run B27 under the preregistered 300 s reserve in case driver.sh's more conservative padded guard (EST=200, RESERVE=330) dropped it. The driver ran B27 itself and no arm was dropped, so the fallback never fired. Its wait loop matched its own launching command line and kept polling; it performed no measurement. runs/dropped.txt was never created, which is the record that no arm was dropped on budget.

PROTOCOL_DEVIATIONS_AND_INCIDENTS.item: A pkill -f in a cleanup command matched its own shell
PROTOCOL_DEVIATIONS_AND_INCIDENTS.detail: An attempt to terminate the idle b27_guarded.sh fallback used `pkill -f b27_guarded.sh`, whose pattern matched the invoking shell's own command line and terminated it (exit 144) before the finalisation step ran. The step was re-run. No measurement was in flight and no run artifact was touched.
